description: I'm a space enthusiast who loves to explore several fields related to space. So feel free to join my team if you're into exploring the unknown as well.
summary:
Ghost Explorers: Stories of NASA's Silent Machines is a free, mobile-friendly web page that brings 13 retired NASA machines back to life through storytelling. These include the Apollo Lunar Module, the Lunar Roving Vehicles, Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity, Viking 1, Ingenuity, Dawn, Pioneer 10 and Kepler. Each explorer tells its own story in the first person. Beside the story, the page shows what the machine looked like, how it worked, the science it made possible, where it rests now, and exact dates and figures from NASA's data archive and mission pages. A read-aloud button and a short quiz help people remember what they learned.
It answers the challenge by turning dense technical records into an engaging, accurate narrative for school-age and casual space fans, with every story linked to its NASA source. It matters because these machines are monuments to over 50 years of exploration, and their stories can inspire the next generation. Anyone can use it with no sign-up.
details:
What it does: Ghost Explorers is a free web page where 13 retired NASA machines on the Moon, Mars and in deep space each tell their own story in the first person. Visitors pick a tab (All, Moon, Mars, Deep space) and tap an explorer. They then see the science it made possible, where it rests now, and a link to its NASA source page. Six explorers also have a diagram, a key-parts list, "how it worked" steps and a table of exact NASA figures. A read-aloud button and a short quiz help people remember what they learned.

Benefits: It's free, needs no sign-up or install, works on phones, and uses plain language for people with no science background.

Intended impact: We want students, families and teachers to feel connected to these machines and inspired by the science behind them.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single page, the browser's built-in read-aloud feature, and Netlify for hosting. We used AI assistance (Claude) to help draft and build the project, then checked the facts against NASA pages.

Creativity: Each machine speaks as a character. Story, drawings, how-it-worked steps and real NASA numbers are combined.

Factors considered: The audience (school-age and casual fans), accuracy (NASA sources only, with the narration labeled as creative), and accessibility (mobile-friendly, large text, read-aloud, no login).
